ai.description: This 50mm gecko is pale grey to sandy brown with dark dorsal crossbands. It features strongly keeled, triangular tubercles on the back and unwebbed, dilated toes with divided subdigital lamellae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus robustus* is best distinguished by its strongly keeled, trihedral dorsal tubercles that are distinctly larger than the interspaces between them.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus robustus* inhabits arid to semi-arid scrublands and rocky outcrops across the Indian subcontinent, typically ranging from sea level to mid-altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Red Sea house gecko is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting insects on vertical surfaces and near artificial lights throughout the night.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus robustus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon and post-monsoon.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus robustus* occurs in the Indian subcontinent primarily along the arid coastal regions of Gujarat and Rajasthan, typically at low elevations.
